title: New rental trend? A $200 'work-from-home fee' tacked on to Bay Area lease
excerpt: A newly built, furnished one-bedroom ADU in Walnut Creek is listed for $3,250 a month with utilities and Wi-Fi included. But the listing also states, "If working from home additional $200 monthly."
content_html:
WALNUT CREEK, Calif. (KGO) -- A Bay Area rental listing is turning heads online, not because of the home itself, but because of one unexpected line.

A newly built, furnished one-bedroom accessory dwelling unit, or ADU, in Walnut Creek is listed for $3,250 a month with utilities and Wi-Fi included. But the listing also states, "If working from home additional $200 monthly."

The optional fee quickly caught the attention of renters, many of whom said they had never heard of anything like it.

"That's crazy," said Bay Area renter Samara Wondimu.

"Work-from-home fee? Nah, I've never heard of that," said Christopher Williams, who works remotely in Chicago.

MORE: 749-square-foot San Jose ADU condo sells for $530K; first-of-its-kind for CA

Another renter, Cody Hall, called the idea "ridiculous."

The listing advertises a 535-square-foot furnished cottage in Walnut Creek's Northgate neighborhood. It includes utilities, internet, a private patio and parking. The additional charge appears to be aimed at tenants who regularly work from home.

"Rent is already so expensive!" Williams said.

He's right. According to Zillow, the average rent across the Bay Area is about $3,650 a month, roughly 81% higher than the national average. For some renters, the possibility of paying another $200 each month only added to the sticker shock.

While unusual, housing experts say the fee is not necessarily out of bounds.

"It's almost like a utility cost recovery or environmental conservation fee," said Derek Barnes, CEO of the East Bay Rental Housing Association.

MORE: AI IPO boom set to transform San Francisco, starting with soaring real estate prices

Barnes said someone working from home throughout the day could use more electricity, water, internet and air conditioning than someone who leaves for an office. He also said ADU owners may have more flexibility than larger apartment buildings, depending on the location and which rent regulations apply.

Barnes does not expect work-from-home fees to become widespread, but said the listing could start a broader conversation about utility use and conservation.

"You're not likely, you know, to be aware of your usage of these precious resources if you don't see a bill," Barnes said.

ABC7 Eyewitness News stopped by by the Walnut Creek property and called the person who posted the listing, but did not receive a response.

For now, renters say they hope the idea does not spread.

"If my landlord suggests that, I actually don't work from home," Hall joked.

content_html_zh:
加利福尼亚州核桃溪 (KGO)——旧金山湾区的一份出租清单在网上引起关注，不是因为房屋本身，而是因为一条意想不到的线路。

核桃溪 (Walnut Creek) 新建的带家具的一居室附属住宅单元 (ADU) 挂牌价为每月 3,250 美元，包含公用设施和 Wi-Fi。 但清单上还注明，“如果在家工作，每月额外支付 200 美元。”

可选费用很快引起了租房者的注意，其中许多人表示他们从未听说过类似的事情。

“这太疯狂了，”湾区租户萨马拉·旺迪姆 (Samara Wondimu) 说。

“在家工作费？ 不，我从来没有听说过，”在芝加哥远程工作的克里斯托弗·威廉姆斯说。

更多信息：749 平方英尺的圣何塞 ADU 公寓售价 53 万美元； CA 首创

另一位租客科迪·霍尔（Cody Hall）称这个想法“荒谬”。

该清单宣传的是核桃溪北门附近一座 535 平方英尺、带家具的小屋。 它包括公用设施、互联网、私人庭院和停车场。 额外费用似乎是针对经常在家工作的租户。

“房租已经这么贵了！” 威廉姆斯说。

他是对的。 根据 Zillow 的数据，湾区的平均租金约为每月 3,650 美元，比全国平均水平高出约 81%。 对于一些租房者来说，每个月还要支付 200 美元的可能性只会让他们更加震惊。

虽然不寻常，但住房专家表示，这笔费用并不一定超出范围。

“这几乎就像公用事业成本回收或环境保护费，”东湾租赁住房协会首席执行官德里克·巴恩斯说。

更多：人工智能 IPO 热潮将改变旧金山，首先是房地产价格飙升

巴恩斯说，全天在家工作的人可能比去办公室工作的人使用更多的电、水、互联网和空调。 他还表示，ADU 业主可能比大型公寓楼拥有更大的灵活性，具体取决于位置和适用的租金法规。

巴恩斯预计在家工作收费不会普及，但表示该清单可能会引发有关公用事业使用和节约的更广泛讨论。

巴恩斯说：“如果你没有看到账单，你就不可能知道你对这些宝贵资源的使用情况。”

ABC7 目击者新闻路过 Walnut Creek 的房产，并给发布该房源的人打电话，但没有收到回复。

目前，租房者表示他们希望这个想法不会蔓延。

“如果我的房东这么建议，我实际上不会在家工作，”霍尔开玩笑说。
